tools.name: list_apis
tools.description: List the APIs and developer platforms this service monitors, optionally filtered by category. Statuses come from the most recently published monitor snapshot, not a live probe, and can be up to a day old — check monitorCheckedAt, and call get_api_status when the caller needs the status right now.

tools.name: search_apis
tools.description: Find monitored APIs by name, slug, category or description. Use this to resolve a product name the user mentioned into the slug the other tools take.

tools.name: get_api_status
tools.description: Probe a monitored API endpoint at call time and return up/degraded/down with the response time. This is the tool to reach for when a user asks "is X down?" — it makes a real request rather than reading the hourly cache.

tools.name: list_down_apis
tools.description: Everything the most recent monitor run found down or degraded, across all categories. Returns an empty list when the monitor snapshot is missing or stale — an empty list is therefore not proof that everything is healthy; check monitorLastRun.

tools.name: get_uptime_history
tools.description: Uptime percentages, response-time stats and recorded data points for one API over a time range. History is retained for 30 days; an API added recently will have few or no data points, which reads as null percentages rather than 100%.

tools.name: get_incident_history
tools.description: Real incidents a vendor published on its own status page, newest first, with start/end times, duration, severity, affected components and a link to the vendor’s incident page. Use this for "has X been flaky lately?" — it is the vendor’s own record, not our probes. Services without a public Statuspag

tools.name: rank_reliability
tools.description: Given several service slugs, return a scorecard ranked worst-first: incident count, total downtime minutes, mean time to resolve, and the longest incident over a window. tools.name: list_categories
tools.description: Category slugs and how many monitored APIs sit in each. Use the slugs with list_apis.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "list_apis" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "List the APIs and developer platforms this service monitors, optionally filtered by category. Statuses are from the most recent hourly monitor run, not a live probe." → after: "List the APIs and developer platforms this service monitors, optionally filtered by category. Statuses come from the most recently published monitor snapshot, not a live probe, and can be up to a day old — check monitorCheckedAt, and call get_api_status when the caller needs the status right now."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
